Subject: New first-position owner-carry note available, Lawrenceville GA, $495K note

Hi, I'm originating a seller-financed note on a 6BR/3BA, 3,650 sqft SFR in Lawrenceville, GA 30043 (Zillow zpid 14802515). Listed at $530K on MLS #10811256, 57 days on market as of September 18 with three cuts already, the latest $50K on 9/17, so I'm motivated to close this month.

Terms are a $495,000 note ($35K buyer down, 6.6% down), 8.5% fixed, 30-year fully amortizing schedule, no balloon. The buyer is fully screened, credit report, verified income, and a written ability-to-repay file. A GA licensed attorney closes it, security deed recorded in first position, third-party loan servicing from day one, full doc package.

Reply with your buy price or call [YOUR PHONE].

objection_handling.response: The opposite, you get the warranty deed at closing and I record a security deed, the same structure a bank uses. A third-party servicer handles payments from day one, so everything reports clean. And I screen for ability to pay, so I'm not handing keys to someone who can't sustain it.

objection_handling.objection: Why is the monthly higher than a bank loan?
objection_handling.response: Because there's no bank, the owner takes the rate risk a lender would. At today's rates around 7%, a conventional loan on this price with 20% down runs about $2,821 P&I but you'd need to qualify, have that $106K down, and pay lender fees. This trades rate for access, and you refinance out whenever you qualify.

objection_handling.objection: The price seems high for the area.
objection_handling.response: Comps in the subdivision sold between $448K and $495K, and the home just had a $50K cut. What you're buying is the financing, not just the house. No lender fees, no PMI, no appraisal wait, and close in 7 to 14 days.

The balloon means the remaining balance is due at year 5. Most buyers refinance into a normal mortgage by then, 5 years of on-time payments builds exactly the track record lenders want to see. If credit is still an issue, we can extend, but the refi path is the plan.

$35K is the floor because it protects both of us, you get real equity from day one and the deal stays fundable. If you have strong income docs I'll present it to the owner, but expect a no under $35K.
